$description: Layout and grid tokens, plus the hero's corrected viewport-relative geometry.

heroGeometry.$description: CORRECTED. CLONE_SPEC.md:186 asserts .hero-dashboard-sticky is a flat 820px tall. That is FALSE — 820px is only the value at viewport height 900, the one height the clone had historically been spot-checked at. Re-measured on live with Playwright at desktop 1280/1440/1600/1920 x 700/800/900/1080 and mobile 375x667, 390x700, 390x844, 390x900, 430x932, 768x1024: every hero dimension tracks the viewport HEIGHT and is independent of viewport WIDTH, holding exactly at all viewports with zero residual.

desktop.anchorTopOffsetExplanation: The clone's sticky is inset 160px where live's is 80px (the clone uses a -80px margin-top under a fixed nav and absorbs both offsets in one padding), so the clone's declared top carries an extra -240px: 50vh - 40 - 240.

mobile.scrollScrubNote: The mobile hero fills exactly one screen, so the scroll range is zero, --progress never advances past 0, and the dashboard clip stays a 48x48 box. This is the real live behaviour, not a degradation.

scrollRange.warning: CLONE_SPEC.md:183 and src/components/Hero.jsx:68 both assert a flat 2060px outer-wrapper height at desktop. Unlike the sticky/landing-hero/clip dimensions, this number was NOT re-measured across viewport heights during the correction pass that produced the viewport-relative rules above. It is internally inconsistent with them: the sticky is 100vh-80px, so the usable scroll range (heroHeight - innerHeight, per src/components/Hero.jsx:39) is 2060 - 100vh, which varies with viewport height rather than being fixed. A generator MUST NOT treat 2060 as a measured constant. Treat the scroll-scrub as 'a pinned range longer than one viewport, exact length unverified'.

sectionMinHeights.$description: Desktop-only floors, each verified in the source as scoped behind min-width:769px or an inline style.
